GAN · VISUAL OVERVIEW

Two networks compete to help generate new examples

The Generator makes synthetic samples. The Discriminator learns to distinguish real data from generated data, supplying feedback during training.

04 · Medium · objective and gradients

Discriminator learns to judge; Generator learns to fool

First understand: The training step for D tries to improve judgment. The next step for G tries to make a more convincing fake.

Original minimax game: minG maxD 𝔼x∼pdata[log D(x)] + 𝔼z∼pz[log(1 − D(G(z)))]
Practical non-saturating Generator loss: −𝔼z[log D(G(z))]. BCE supplies the classification terms; optimizers alternate.

questions.figure:
05 · Medium · build in PyTorch

Two networks, two optimizers, one digit image task

Practical idea: Train D on real versus fake, then train G to fool D. Repeat and save image samples after epochs.

# Key PyTorch training pattern
fake = G(z)

# Update D with real and detached fake
loss_d = bce(D(real), ones) + bce(D(fake.detach()), zeros)
opt_d.zero_grad()
loss_d.backward()
opt_d.step()

# Update G to fool D
loss_g = bce(D(G(z)), ones)
opt_g.zero_grad()
loss_g.backward()
opt_g.step()
Training checkpoint

MNIST contains 28×28 digit images. Normalize pixels to match the Generator’s Tanh output.

Save samples from fixed noise so changes across epochs are comparable.

The eight illustrated digits in the diagram are not actual model outputs.

Show complete runnable MNIST PyTorch example
# pip install torch torchvision
import torch
from torch import nn
from torchvision import datasets, transforms, utils
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
z_dim = 64

G = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Linear(z_dim, 128), nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(128, 256), nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(256, 784), nn.Tanh()
).to(device)

D = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Flatten(),
    nn.Linear(784, 256), nn.LeakyReLU(0.2),
    nn.Linear(256, 1)
).to(device)

dataset = datasets.MNIST(
    "data", train=True, download=True,
    transform=transforms.Compose([
        transforms.ToTensor(),
        transforms.Normalize((0.5,), (0.5,))
    ])
)
loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=128, shuffle=True)
criterion = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss()
opt_g = torch.optim.Adam(G.parameters(), lr=0.0002)
opt_d = torch.optim.Adam(D.parameters(), lr=0.0002)
fixed_z = torch.randn(16, z_dim, device=device)

for epoch in range(3):
    for real, _ in loader:
        real = real.to(device)
        n = real.size(0)
        z = torch.randn(n, z_dim, device=device)

        # 1. Train the Discriminator.
        fake = G(z)
        loss_d = (criterion(D(real), torch.ones(n, 1, device=device))
               + criterion(D(fake.detach()), torch.zeros(n, 1, device=device)))
        opt_d.zero_grad()
        loss_d.backward()
        opt_d.step()

        # 2. Train the Generator through D.
        loss_g = criterion(D(G(z)), torch.ones(n, 1, device=device))
        opt_g.zero_grad()
        loss_g.backward()
        opt_g.step()

    # Preview the same latent inputs after each epoch.
    with torch.no_grad():
        samples = (G(fixed_z).reshape(-1, 1, 28, 28) + 1) / 2
        utils.save_image(samples, f"gan_epoch_{epoch + 1}.png", nrow=4)
    print(epoch + 1, round(loss_d.item(), 3), round(loss_g.item(), 3))
